Rafael Moretti-Klein
Backend Engineer | Python, Go
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer and technical leader with experience designing and building production services in Go and Python. Work includes high-throughput entitlement services, Python and Go service migration, API reliability, and observability on GCP and Kubernetes. Now focused on hands-on individual-contributor backend engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go, C++
Backend and APIs: FastAPI, gRPC, playback API development
Data and storage: Cassandra, Redis, BigQuery
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP, GKE, Kubernetes, Terraform
Observability: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus
Testing: pytest, tox

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–2026
Director of Engineering | 2019–2026
- Led the platform organisation of 45 engineers.
- Built an internal cloud cost dashboard using BigQuery billing exports, Looker Studio and Python scripts; rightsizing and committed-use discounts saved EUR 4.2M per year (31%).
- Contributed to the monolith-to-services migration, moving a Python 2 monolith toward approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE.
- Established a service template using FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and Terraform modules.
- Improved playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.

Principal Engineer | 2015–2019
- Served as technical lead for the playback API.
- Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service handling subscriptions, regions and devices; it handled 120,000 requests per second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms.
- Used Cassandra with local in-memory caching for the entitlement service.

SELECTED ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Open-source maintainer | Python retry library | 2012–2018
- Maintained a small Python retry library with approximately 1,500 GitHub stars; handed over maintenance in 2018.
- Used pytest and tox.

Co-inventor | Granted German patent | 2013
- Co-inventor of a method for adaptive GPS sampling in vehicle fleets, using driving context to reduce GPS data volume.
- Technologies: C++, statistics.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise engineering CV with a clear target profile, relevant technologies, and unusually credible quantified results. The entitlement service metrics, 99.95% availability result, service-migration scale, and EUR 4.2M annual savings create strong evidence of impact. The structure is easy to scan and the move from Director of Engineering to Principal Engineer makes the technical progression understandable. The main content weaknesses are that the document does not show several requirements from the advert—most notably relational databases, REST APIs, Docker, and CI/CD—and the current employment dates do not reflect the candidate’s stated August 2026 departure. These are partly candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, plain text bullets, and strong ATS keywords including Python, Go, FastAPI, GCP, GKE, Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, pytest, and Cassandra. Its AI-screening probability is good for Python backend, FastAPI, cloud deployment, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, observability, automated testing, and high-scale API reliability. Screening performance will be weaker for exact terms such as PostgreSQL, relational databases, query tuning, schema migrations, REST APIs, Docker, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, Kafka, and AWS. The document should not add those terms without supporting evidence. The [EMAIL] and [PHONE] placeholders are also a practical ATS and recruiter-usability problem.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong match for the backend-service, Python/FastAPI, cloud, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, testing, API-reliability, and architecture aspects of the role. The Python 2-to-Python 3 migration and approximately 60-service platform are relevant evidence of substantial Python service experience, while the Go entitlement service satisfies the comparable-language route. The candidate’s transition back to hands-on individual-contributor work is clearly stated and aligns with the role. The CV does not establish relational database experience, PostgreSQL, query tuning, schema migrations, REST API design or consumption, Docker, CI/CD, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, logistics/EDI knowledge, or Dutch/French. AWS-specific experience is also not demonstrated, although the must-have wording accepts deployment to a cloud environment and the CV shows GCP/GKE experience. These are candidate-profile gaps or unverified areas, not defects that should be addressed by adding unsupported claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the contact line at the top of the CV, replace [EMAIL] and [PHONE] with the candidate’s actual email address and phone number, and replace [LINKEDIN] with the complete LinkedIn URL if a profile is intended to be provided. Do not submit application placeholders.

CRITICAL — In the Professional Experience section, change “Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–2026” to “Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–Aug 2026” and change “Director of Engineering | 2019–2026” to “Director of Engineering | 2019–Aug 2026” so the CV accurately reflects the candidate’s stated departure after the August 2026 reorganization.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary, change “Now focused on hands-on individual-contributor backend engineering” to “Seeking hands-on individual-contributor backend engineering work” to make the career objective more direct and application-oriented without implying current employment.

MINOR — In the Principal Engineer subsection, revise the entitlement-service bullet to include the supported Redis detail: “Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service handling subscriptions, regions and devices; it handled 120,000 requests per second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms, using Cassandra and Redis-backed local in-memory caching.” This makes the existing Redis skill more visible in an achievement bullet. Ensure the wording accurately reflects the implementation.

MINOR — In the Director of Engineering subsection, consider placing the two technically strongest bullets—the Python 2-to-Python 3/Go service migration and the FastAPI/Go service template—before the organisation-leadership bullet. This will make the CV’s hands-on backend relevance visible earlier to recruiters screening for an individual-contributor role, while retaining the leadership experience.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The contact details contain unresolved placeholders ([EMAIL], [PHONE], and [LINKEDIN]), which can prevent recruiter contact and reduce application usability. Fix: replace them with the candidate’s real contact details before submission.
2. The CV presents Streamhaus employment as continuing through 2026, while the candidate’s original notes state that they left in August 2026. Fix: use “Aug 2026” in both the company and Director of Engineering date ranges.
No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected when compared with the Original Candidate Information.

Seeking hands-on individual-contributor backend engineering work.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go, C++

Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–Aug 2026
Director of Engineering | 2019–Aug 2026
- Contributed to the monolith-to-services migration, moving a Python 2 monolith toward approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE.

Principal Engineer | 2015–2019

- Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service using gRPC, handling subscriptions, regions and devices; it handled 120,000 requests per second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms, using Cassandra and Redis-backed local in-memory caching.

SELECTED ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Open-source maintainer | Python retry library | 2012–2018
- Maintained a small Python retry library with approximately 1,500 GitHub stars; handed over maintenance in 2018.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is concise, professional, and well structured. It presents strong quantified achievements, including 120,000 requests per second, p99 latency below 15 ms, 99.95% API availability, approximately 60 services, leadership of 45 engineers, and EUR 4.2M in annual savings. The progression from Principal Engineer to Director of Engineering is clear, and the stated objective of returning to hands-on individual-contributor backend work is relevant to the role. The main content weakness is that the CV emphasizes senior leadership and platform-scale accomplishments more than recent hands-on Python implementation. It also does not explicitly distinguish production backend engineering from organisational leadership, which may make the candidate appear overqualified or less aligned with a small-team IC role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly section headings, plain text formatting, standard bullets, recognizable technology names, and no apparent tables, graphics, headers, or parsing obstacles. Strong searchable terms include Python, Go, FastAPI, gRPC, GKE, Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, pytest, tox, Cassandra, Redis, and BigQuery. AI and keyword screening probability is good for Python/backend, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, cloud, API reliability, and automated testing, but materially weaker for the role's explicit must-have terms: PostgreSQL, relational databases, query tuning, schema migrations, REST APIs, Docker, CI/CD, and AWS. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than wording defects where the original material does not support them. The phrase "infrastructure as code." should be normalized to "infrastructure as code" without a trailing full stop for consistency, but this is minor.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV strongly matches the requirement for more than three years of backend experience in Python or a comparable language, and it is particularly strong for Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, API reliability, cloud deployment on GCP, and high-throughput services. FastAPI experience is directly relevant to the advertised Python service stack. The entitlement service and playback API demonstrate strong performance, reliability, and technical trade-off experience. However, the candidate's material does not support PostgreSQL, relational database design, query tuning, schema migrations, Docker, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, logistics or EDI knowledge, or Dutch/French language skills. The material also does not establish CI/CD, AWS depth, REST API work specifically, on-call participation, incident post-mortems, or design-note practices. The CV therefore aligns well with the backend, reliability, cloud, Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, and observability aspects of the role, but only partially with several mandatory implementation requirements. The leadership background and stated return to IC work are credible, although the document should make the recent hands-on scope more prominent.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the hands-on backend focus more explicit without overstating recent coding activity. Replace the opening with wording such as: "Backend engineer and technical leader with 11+ years building production services in Python and Go, including approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services deployed on GKE. Experience includes FastAPI service templates, high-throughput entitlement services, API reliability, cloud cost tooling in Python, and observability with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus. Seeking senior or staff-level individual-contributor backend engineering work." This better matches the target role while remaining supported by the candidate information.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Backend and APIs: FastAPI, gRPC, playback API development, API reliability" to "Backend and APIs: FastAPI, gRPC, API design, API reliability, playback API development." "API design" is supported by designing the entitlement service and leading the playback API, while this wording does not incorrectly imply REST experience.

3. In the Technical Skills section, change "Testing: pytest, tox" to "Testing: automated testing, pytest, tox." The open-source experience explicitly supports automated testing, and this improves matching for the testing requirement without claiming CI/CD experience.

4. In the Professional Experience section under Streamhaus GmbH, make the production Python scope easier to identify by changing "Contributed to the monolith-to-services migration, moving a Python 2 monolith toward approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE" to "Contributed to a strangler-fig migration of a Python 2 monolith toward approximately 60 production Python 3 and Go services deployed on GKE." The term "strangler-fig" is supported by the candidate portfolio, and "production" accurately reflects the service migration context.

5. In the Director of Engineering subsection, keep the cost-dashboard bullet but clarify its hands-on implementation: change "Built an internal cloud cost dashboard using BigQuery billing exports, Looker Studio and Python scripts" to "Built Python scripts and an internal cloud cost dashboard using BigQuery billing exports and Looker Studio." This places the supported Python implementation work earlier and makes it more relevant to a Python backend screening process.

6. In the Selected Additional Experience section, change "Applied automated testing with pytest and tox" to "Applied automated testing using pytest and tox to validate the Python retry library." This is more concrete and improves keyword matching while staying within the original evidence.

7. In the Professional Experience section, add a short scope line immediately below the Streamhaus dates or before the role entries: "Progressed from Principal Engineer to Director of Engineering; returned to the job market in August 2026 seeking hands-on individual-contributor backend work." This clarifies the transition and prevents the Director title from obscuring the target IC positioning. Do not add claims about Docker, PostgreSQL, REST, CI/CD, AWS, Kafka, or on-call work because they are not supported by the candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, metrics-driven CV with a clear backend engineering positioning. The entitlement service, migration, availability, and cost-saving achievements demonstrate substantial technical impact. The decision to explain the transition from engineering leadership back to hands-on individual-contributor work is useful and credible. The main content limitation is that several requirements central to this role are either not demonstrated or are only partially represented: relational databases/PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Docker, and CI/CD. The CV also provides limited evidence of code review, incident response, documentation, or explaining technical trade-offs, although some architecture and reliability work is evident.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, simple text formatting, conventional bullet points, and relevant keywords including Python, FastAPI, Go, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, pytest, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry. It should parse reliably and has a good keyword match for the role's Python, FastAPI, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, testing, and cloud requirements. AI screening probability is moderate to high for the supported backend requirements, but likely lower for exact must-have searches involving PostgreSQL, relational databases, REST, Docker, CI/CD, and AWS. Do not add those keywords unless supported by actual experience. The Skills section could also be more precise: 'Python' and 'Python 3' are redundant, while supported technologies such as gRPC and Redis are not connected to the relevant project bullets or are not fully surfaced.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's backend-service, Python migration, FastAPI, cloud deployment, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, reliability, and automated-testing themes. The Go entitlement service is a strong comparable-language qualification and the migration work demonstrates meaningful Python production exposure. Kubernetes/Terraform and Prometheus/OpenTelemetry are particularly good nice-to-have matches. The candidate's material does not establish solid relational database or PostgreSQL experience, query tuning, schema migrations, Docker, REST API design/consumption, CI/CD, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, logistics/EDI knowledge, or Dutch/French skills. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved by wording. The CV does provide clear written evidence of technical communication through its description of architecture, migration, reliability, and cost work, but it does not explicitly document spoken English.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified. The CV does not appear to contain unsupported skills or experiences when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, replace the current summary with a more role-focused version such as: "Backend engineer and former engineering leader with 3+ years of professional Python backend experience through a Python 2-to-3 monolith migration and FastAPI service development, alongside substantial production Go experience. Built and operated high-throughput services, improved API reliability, and deployed services on GKE with Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, and Prometheus. Returning to hands-on individual-contributor backend engineering." This preserves the existing claims while placing the strongest supported job keywords earlier.
2. In the Technical Skills section, remove the redundant entry "Python 3" after "Python" and reorganize the supported skills as: "Languages: Python, Go, C++"; "Frameworks and APIs: FastAPI, gRPC, playback API development"; "Data and storage: Cassandra, Redis, BigQuery"; "Cloud and infrastructure: GCP, GKE, Kubernetes, Terraform"; "Observability: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus"; "Testing: pytest, tox." This makes gRPC and Redis easier for ATS and recruiters to find without introducing unsupported technologies.
3. In the Streamhaus experience section, add the project dates already provided in the candidate material to the relevant bullets. For example, label the migration bullet "2019–2023" and the cost-dashboard bullet "2023–2024." This makes the Python experience timeline more explicit and supports the stated 3+ years of Python backend work.
4. In the Principal Engineer section, revise the entitlement-service bullet to include the supported technologies from the project record: "Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service using gRPC, Cassandra, Redis, Kubernetes, and local in-memory caching; handled 120,000 requests per second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms." This gives the strongest backend project a more complete and ATS-readable technology context.
5. In the Director of Engineering section, make the migration bullet more explicit about the Python work by changing it to: "Contributed to the 2019–2023 strangler-fig migration of a Python 2 monolith into approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services deployed on GKE." This uses terminology present in the candidate portfolio and more directly matches the job's Python-service requirement.
6. In the Open-source experience section, make the testing evidence more prominent by changing the bullet to: "Maintained and tested a Python retry library with pytest and tox from 2012–2018; the project reached approximately 1,500 GitHub stars before maintenance was handed over." This more directly supports the automated-testing requirement.
7. At the top of the CV, add the candidate's actual contact details and any existing professional profile or portfolio links, if available. Use plain text labels such as email, phone, city/country, LinkedIn, and GitHub; do not add links or details that were not supplied or do not exist.
